cards.front: Simplify 24:36
cards.say: Simplify twenty four to thirty six. two to three. Divide both parts by twelve.

cards.front: Simplify 45:60
cards.say: Simplify forty five to sixty. three to four. Divide both parts by fifteen.

cards.front: Simplify 0.5:2
cards.back: 1:4. Multiply both parts by 2 to get 1:4.
cards.say: Simplify zero point five to two. one to four. Multiply both parts by two to get one to four.

cards.front: Share 56 in the ratio 3:4
cards.back: 24 and 32. There are 7 parts and 56 ÷ 7 = 8, so 3 × 8 = 24 and 4 × 8 = 32.
cards.say: Share fifty six in the ratio three to four. twenty four and thirty two. There are seven parts and fifty six divided by seven equals eight, so three times eight equals twenty four and four times eight equals thirty two.

cards.front: Share 90 in the ratio 2:3:4
cards.say: Share ninety in the ratio two to three to four. twenty, thirty and forty. There are nine parts and ninety divided by nine equals ten.

cards.front: Red and blue beads are in the ratio 3:5. There are 15 red. How many blue?
cards.back: 25. Each part is 15 ÷ 3 = 5, so blue is 5 × 5 = 25.
cards.say: Red and blue beads are in the ratio three to five. There are fifteen red. How many blue? twenty five. Each part is fifteen divided by three equals five, so blue is five times five equals twenty five.

cards.front: If the ratio of boys to girls is 2:3, what fraction are girls?
cards.back: 3/5. There are 5 parts in total and 3 are girls.
cards.say: If the ratio of boys to girls is two to three, what fraction are girls? three fifths. There are five parts in total and three are girls.

cards.front: 12 biscuits need 150 g of flour. How much flour for 20 biscuits?
cards.back: 250 g. One biscuit needs 12.5 g, so 20 need 20 × 12.5 = 250 g.
cards.say: Twelve biscuits need one hundred and fifty grams of flour. How much for twenty biscuits? Two hundred and fifty grams. One biscuit needs twelve point five grams.

cards.front: 5 m of ribbon costs 35 dollars. What do 8 m cost?
cards.back: 56 dollars. 1 m costs 7 dollars, so 8 m cost 8 × 7 = 56.
cards.say: five metres of ribbon costs thirty five dollars. What do eight metres cost? fifty six dollars. one metre costs seven dollars, so eight metres cost eight times seven equals fifty six.

cards.front: A map has scale 1:50,000. How far is 1 cm on the map in real life?
cards.say: A map has scale one to fifty thousand. How far is one centimetre on the map in real life? fifty thousand centimetres, which is five hundred metres.

cards.front: A drawing has scale 1:100. A line is 3 cm on the drawing. How long is the real thing?
cards.say: A drawing has scale one to one hundred. A line is three centimetres on the drawing. How long is the real thing? three hundred centimetres, which is three metres.

cards.front: What does a scale of 1:10 mean?
cards.back: Real lengths are 10 times as long as the lengths on the drawing.
cards.say: What does a scale of one to ten mean? Real lengths are ten times as long as the lengths on the drawing.
fifteen per cent of eighty. twelve. ten per cent is eight and five per cent is four, so eight plus four equals twelve.
thirty per cent of two hundred and fifty. seventy five. ten per cent is twenty five, so thirty per cent is three times twenty five equals seventy five.
twelve point five per cent of sixty four. eight. twelve point five per cent is one eighth, and sixty four divided by eight equals eight.
seventy five per cent of thirty six. twenty seven. twenty five per cent is nine, so seventy five per cent is three times nine equals twenty seven.

cards.back: 4.5. 10% is 9, so 5% is half of that.
cards.say: five per cent of ninety. four point five. ten per cent is nine, so five per cent is half of that.

cards.front: How can you find 1% of an amount?
cards.say: How can you find one per cent of an amount? Divide by one hundred. Example: one per cent of five hundred is five.

cards.front: A coat costs 60 dollars. It has 20% off. What is the sale price?
cards.say: A coat costs sixty dollars. It has twenty per cent off. What is the sale price? forty eight dollars. twenty per cent of sixty is twelve, and sixty minus twelve equals forty eight.

cards.front: A jacket costs 120 dollars. It has 25% off. What is the sale price?
cards.say: A jacket costs one hundred and twenty dollars. It has twenty five per cent off. What is the sale price? ninety dollars. twenty five per cent of one hundred and twenty is thirty, and one hundred and twenty minus thirty equals ninety.

cards.front: A price of 40 dollars goes up by 10%. What is the new price?
cards.say: A price of forty dollars goes up by ten per cent. What is the new price? forty four dollars. ten per cent of forty is four, and forty plus four equals forty four.

cards.front: 18 out of 24 as a percentage
cards.say: eighteen out of twenty four as a percentage. seventy five per cent. eighteen twenty fourths equals three quarters equals seventy five per cent.

cards.front: 35 out of 50 as a percentage
cards.say: thirty five out of fifty as a percentage. seventy per cent. thirty five fiftieths equals seventy hundredths.

cards.front: A price rises from 80 to 100 dollars. What is the percentage increase?
cards.say: A price rises from eighty to one hundred dollars. What is the percentage increase? twenty five per cent. The rise is twenty and twenty eightieths equals one quarter equals twenty five per cent.
